questions.question: Directions: In the following question, a statement is given followed by two conclusions/assumptions. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions/assumptions, if any, follow from the given statement. Statement: If people are intelligent they are also creative. Assumptions: I. Creativity and intelligence are related. II. Creative people are intelligent.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the following question, a statement is given followed by two conclusions/assumptions. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions/assumptions, if any, follow from the given statement.

Statement: If people are intelligent they are also creative.

Assumptions:

I. Creativity and intelligence are related.

II. Creative people are intelligent.

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are invalid.
options.html: Both assumptions I and II are invalid.

options.text: Only assumption I is valid.
options.html: Only assumption I is valid.

options.text: Only assumption II is valid
options.html: Only assumption II is valid

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are valid.
options.html: Both assumptions I and II are valid.

questions.solution:
The statement says that intelligent people are creative, hence it indicates that there is a relation between creativity and intelligence. Therefore, assumption I follows. 

The statement does not give us any information that people who are creative will also be intelligent. Therefore, assumption II does not follow. 

The correct option is (2).

questions.question: A question is given followed by two arguments numbered I and II. you have to decide which of the arguments is a ‘strong’ argument. Question: Should the people of India pay taxes to the government? Arguments: I. Yes, taxes have to be paid to the government to run the country. II. No, taxes need not to be paid, as a person has to look after his/her needs first.

questions.solution:
Argument I states that taxes are ‘needed’ by the government for the country’s administration and hence can be considered a strong argument.

Argument II comes across as an excuse and is not applicable on the citizens who can afford to pay the taxes. Therefore, argument II is not strong.

questions.solution:
Given,

Statement: As a step towards reducing the number of smokers and alcoholics, for the last four-five years, the censor board has been insisting on removing scenes involving smoking and drinking in films.

1.People are inspired by movies to smoke and drink. Mostly people inspired by the movies so we can consider the 1st argument.

2. Four-five years ago, people were not influenced by movies to smoke and drink. This statement can not be considered.

3.The censor board also has some social responsibilities. This statement can be considered because it is a social responsibility of the censor board to aware people about drinking and smoking.

Hence, 'Only arguments I and III are strong' is the correct answer.

Statements: A cinema hall has kept some video games to keep its audience busy during the weekend. Assumptions: I. People like to play video games. II. questions.solution:
Given data :

Statements: A cinema hall has kept some video games to keep its audience busy during the weekend.   

Assumptions:

I. People like to play video games → Yes, it can be concluded from the given statement because this is the reason behind the cinema hall arranged some video games during the weekend.

II. People will like the movie playing in the theater → No, it can not be concluded from the given statement because the statement is all about the arrangement of video games.

Hence, 'only assumption I is implicit' is the correct answer.

Assumptions: I. The schools do not admit children after 6 years of age. II. Below the age of 5 a child does not attain appropriate level of development and ability to learn.

questions.solution:
Given: A child should be put in school at the age of 5 years or so.

Explanation:

As per the statement, it only tells us that the child can go to school at the age of 5. It means that the child is mentally prepared at this age only and not before that. So, II is implicit.

Since nothing is mentioned about the admission or school policy after 6 years in the given statement. So, I is not implicit.

Thus, only assumption II is implicit.

Hence, 'option 4' is correct.

questions.solution:
The question simply asks whether hunting of lions should be banned.

  • Argument 1 states that hunting of lions should be banned because it requires a lot of money. It is not logically correct, because it cannot be determined if the fact is true and more importantly, it is not a fair justification to ban hunting. Thus, argument 1 is not strong.
  • Argument 2 does not give a reason as to why hunting of lions should not be banned. Thus, it is not making any point to be strong.

Hence the correct answer is option 4.

Read both the statements and give answer. (A) : The prices of fruits have dropped substantially during the last few days. (B) : The prices of foodgrains have increased substantially during the last few days.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In each of these questions are given two statements (A) and (B) These statements may be either independent causes or may be effects of independent causes or of a common cause. Read both the statements and give answer.

(A) : The prices of fruits have dropped substantially during the last few days.

(B) : The prices of foodgrains have increased substantially during the last few days.

options.html: If statement (B) is the cause and statement (A) is its effect.

questions.solution:
Statement (A) and (B) are effects of some independent cause.

The price of fruits have dropped is not related to the price of food grains increased is nowhere related to common cause. 

They are the effects of the independent causes.

Hence, the correct answer is "if both statements are effects of independent causes". 

Additional Information

What are Causes?

Causes are the conditions under which an event occurs.

For example, can you guess the causes for the following? 

The police increasing security around the President's house.

Lots of people buying a particular expensive brand of washing machines around Diwali. Easily, we can guess causes for the above events. 

There were reports of threats against the President. 

There was a high discount or sale for that brand during Diwali.

Sufficient & Necessary Conditions:

In a cause and effect question, the cause is the sufficient condition. It is assumed that the sufficient condition of the occurrence of the events must include the different necessary conditions as well. 

A necessary condition is one that must be satisfied for the occurrence of an event. 

E.g. You must adhere to the deadline to get your work appraised. 

This means if you get your work appraised, you have to adhere to the deadline. Or; if you do not do not adhere to the deadline, you do not get your work appraised. 

A condition is called a sufficient condition if in a certain event, you are satisfied with the results.

E.g. Being human is a sufficient condition for being a mammal. The act of being a human is not possible unless one is also a mammal. But it is not necessary that being human is a necessary condition for being a mammal.
